needle: Old Mr. Tredgold kept a tame heron in the walled orchard behind his house at Marlowby, and fed it every dusk upon salted herring.

needle: Captain Aldous Merrow lost his left hand to a fishing-boat's winch in the autumn of 1847, and thereafter wore a hook of polished brass.

needle: Young Tobias Fenwick-Gray was thought by the whole neighbourhood to have the sweetest tenor voice in the district, though he sang only at funerals.

query: Which elderly lady has remained rooted in one spot her whole life?

query: Which tiller of the soil appears to have given up his former occupation?

query: Which lady has almost no free evenings in the working week?

query: At the ball, which girl partnered the junior clergyman more than once?

query: Whose carriage broke down on the way to town?

query: Who made an offer of marriage that was declined by the lady?

query: Who was disinherited following a quarrel with his father?

query: Who hosted a dinner for the neighbours at Christmas?

query: Who undertook a long journey across the Channel to spend the cold months abroad?
